isabel: quick thread to finalize a handful of dark-mode polish items before ship: 1) microchart stroke visibility at small sizes, 2) inline vs block code contrast balance, 3) a short copy tweak in the model selector tooltip. vik: paste the current token set so i can run a10y checks locally. ravi: also flag: when charts have gradient backgrounds the legend can get lost. we should try a subtle divider or translucent backdrop. isabel: current tokens snapshot: ``` --bg: #050607 --panel: #0b0d0f --panel-alt: #121315 --muted-txt: #95a0a2 --accent-cool: #64bfff --accent-warm: #ffb38a --inline-code-bg: #090a0b --inline-code-fg: #dbeefc --code-block-bg: #0b0d0f --focus-ring: rgba(110,160,255,0.12) ``` vik: thanks. `inline-code-fg` on `inline-code-bg` is marginal around 4.2:1. contrast-bot will mark it. i'd prefer bumping fg a touch to `#eaf9ff` rather than changing bg so screenshots stay consistent. contrast-bot: automated check: `#dbeefc` on `#090a0b` = 4.2:1 (recommended >=4.5 for regular text). suggestion: `#eaf9ff` => 4.7:1. ravi: for microcharts: idea is to keep stroke 1px but add a micro-halo (subtle glow) and a fallback thicker stroke for non-hardware accelerated contexts. Something like `stroke-width:1; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px rgba(255,255,255,0.055))` and an opt-in `stroke-width:1.2px` variant. anna: i like halo approach. it preserves the thin aesthetic but improves legibility on low-dpi and low-brightness screens. also we should avoid increasing saturation across the board since that shifts brand tone. isabel: legend solutions: A) per-item pills (floats) B) single translucent bar behind the legend C) thin outline under legend items. Which reduces occlusion for overlays? ravi: B is my vote. Full-width translucent bar (panel color with ~0.8 alpha) keeps content readable without creating heavy contrast islands. Also add dividers between items for scannability. vik: small accessibility nit: focus ring alpha is low. bumping to 0.18 and +1px spread helps keyboard users. i propose `--focus-ring: rgba(110,160,255,0.18)`. contrast-bot: note: proposed focus ring change improves perceived focus on `--panel` and `--panel-alt` backgrounds. run `design-kit color-a11y` after token edits. anna: copy tweak: model selector tooltip currently reads "Pick a model" 0 new wording suggestion: "Choose a model for serving (runtime may vary)"? short and sets expectation about runtime differences. isabel: i worry about translation cost. maybe shorter: "Choose a model (runtime varies)". keeps it compact. ravi: +1 for shorter string. also add a brief tooltip under advanced settings that explains quantization vs full precision in one line. isabel: agreed. action items: 1) vik to run color checks and update inline token to `#eaf9ff` if it passes (today). 2) ravi to prototype micro-halo + 1.2px fallback and legend bar sample in storybook (EOD). 3) anna to update tooltip copy key to "Choose a model (runtime varies)" and add the quant note in the advanced tooltip. 4) me to write a one-paragraph rationale in /docs/accessibility linking the contrast report. vik: quick local snippet to test inline token change: ```
const token = 'ok'
``` ravi: micro-halo CSS to test: ``` .sparkline path { stroke-width:1; stroke:var(--accent-cool); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px rgba(255,255,255,0.055)); shape-rendering:geometricPrecision } .sparkline.fallback-thick path { stroke-width:1.2 } ``` contrast-bot: reminder: run `npm run color-a11y --report` in design-kit and attach results to PRs. anna: i'll add the copy PR and ping localization for comments. keep the tooltip string short to minimize translation work. isabel: tiny accessibility note: please include pattern/dash fallback for critical error series so color isn't the only cue. add the pattern spec in the chart component docs. ravi: will include dashed line + diagonal hatch SVG pattern example in the storybook mock. vik: i'll run the a11y report and post results here. if `#eaf9ff` is green, i'll open a tokens PR. isabel: great, thanks everyone 0 will follow up with the docs blurb and PR links in this thread. :sparkles:
